title: proof_coverage's clause-3 tooth counts an outcomes plan as an amendment
intention: ab32ccdc4504's clause-3 tooth treats a ticket that has gained an outcomes plan since its snapshot as amended, and does not compare it.
why: Measured 2026-11-22 on house main: clause 3 of test_clause_keys_come_from_falsifier_clauses.py is red over 15b80c0c393c, 201a37bf1613, 5a4ec289bf15 and d421051bc1f7, each re-keyed to []. Each carries an outcomes plan with no claim (11, 22, 25, 16 outcomes), so pc.clauses keys it on its claimed outcomes, none, as 6e41b8d2f0a3 designed. The tooth skips a ticket only when its falsifier_sha changed; the outcomes migration (aa3e9a70db47) left the falsifier alone, so the reshaped ticket is compared against its 2026-11-05 keys.
traces_to: Law 9 (red is the default; green is earned) and Law 3: a tooth that reds a designed answer measures the wrong thing; the fix makes its own 'amended since the snapshot' test see the plan-shape change.
how: The tooth's skip condition gains plan.has_outcomes(t): the snapshot predates outcomes plans, so a ticket carrying one has changed shape since. A synthetic tooth shows an outcomes ticket is skipped; the existing synthetic teeth and the 90% floor stay. PROVES gains this ticket's clause 1 on the same tooth; the docstring's clause (3) names this ticket.
